source: hand-authored fixture for issue #269 — not shipped data
description: Shapes about what CORROBORATES a self-named allergy rule's bare-containment match, for the injected record's patient-specific reading. (1) 'Ketoconazole' is an entry's own DISPLAY name, so findImpliedSubstances('Ketoconazole') stops there and the equal-claimant leg admits only entries whose claim on the whole recorded name is as strong (NAME_IS_THE_DISPLAY_NAME). (2) Levoketoconazole merely ALIASES 'ketoconazole' and files a self-named allergy rule on that token, so an allergy recorded as 'Ketoconazole' does NOT put its substance in the allergen arm's set — while the record IS a clinician-entered name that names the entry, which is the shape that separates the two corroborating questions and the one a set-only reading hedges wrongly. (3) It also files a second self-named rule on its own name 'levo', which no other entry's name contains and which an allergy recorded as 'Levocetirizine' reaches only mid-word with a six-letter tail — so two rules of ONE collapsed key can disagree about corroboration, which is what the max per key is for. (4) The two Amphotericin B rows both alias 'amphotericin b' and NEITHER is called it, so an allergy recorded under that bare name TIES them: findImpliedSubstances reaches both while findNamedSubstances admits neither (no label occurs in the recorded name, no row is the unique strongest claimant, and nothing is derived). The deoxycholate row rules on another of its own names, 'deoxy', which that allergen does not contain — so the naming record is not one of the rule's witnesses and only the IMPLIED reading can corroborate it. That is the one arrangement separating findImpliedSubstances from findNamedSubstances at this gate. (5) Tramadol files one rule for each section of the reading at once, each with a distinct note: a SELF-NAMED allergy rule on 'trama' that an allergen recorded as 'Tramazoline' reaches only mid-word and neither corroborating question can reach; a CLASS-token rule on 'nsaid' that an allergen recorded as 'NSAIDs' matches and that is not self-named, so it is corroborated by construction; and a condition rule nothing matches. It is the only entry here whose record carries all three sections together, which is what pins their order. (6) Codeine files an allergy rule and a CONDITION rule carrying the SAME note, so the two land on different collapsed keys and render one clause string; with an allergy recorded as 'Dihydrocodeine' (which contains 'codeine' but does not name the entry) the allergy rule is uncorroborated while the condition rule is simply not recorded, which is the cross-key precedence between those two sections. No entry carries ATC codes, so no class comparison can chip and every count is the allergy arms' own.
